fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to say to Pharaoh, Egypt's king, "…I will send swarms of flies upon you and your officials and your people and your houses." (Exodus 8:21) He spells out who and where, right down to the houses. Picture a hot day with the bakery door propped open, then picture that times a whole country.

Locusts are a creepy-crawly guess, baker, but that's not what the LORD says here. He says "…swarms of flies…" (Exodus 8:21) And flies are what pour into Pharaoh's palace in this passage (Exodus 8:24). Swarms, yes. Flies, that's the answer.

Right on the money. The LORD says, "…the land of Goshen, where My people live; no swarms of flies will be found there." (Exodus 8:22) He calls it special treatment. I'd like to see the sign on that neighborhood.

Not the officials, baker. Their houses are where the swarms pour in (Exodus 8:24). Goshen gets different treatment, because the LORD says "…no swarms of flies will be found there." (Exodus 8:22) The people who live there are the ones He calls "My people."

You've got it. The LORD says, "In this way you will know that I, the LORD, am in the land." (Exodus 8:22) The sign is that no swarms are found in Goshen, while swarms ruin the land throughout Egypt (Exodus 8:24). A difference that plain doesn't need a speech.

Hiding is a natural thought, baker, but the LORD never gives it as His reason. What He says is "In this way you will know that I, the LORD, am in the land." (Exodus 8:22) The reason is about Pharaoh knowing the LORD is there.

Sneaky one, friend, but no. Pharaoh says, "Go, sacrifice to your God within this land." (Exodus 8:25) Moses answers, "It would not be right to do that…" (Exodus 8:26) His reason is that the sacrifices would be detestable to the Egyptians.

Goshen is where the LORD's people live, but Moses doesn't name it as the place. He says they must make "…a three-day journey into the wilderness…" (Exodus 8:27) The place is the wilderness, and the sacrifice is to happen "…as He commands us." Goshen isn't the answer.

Moses doesn't name a river in his answer, baker. He says they must go on "…a three-day journey into the wilderness…" (Exodus 8:27) The LORD does mention Pharaoh going out to the water (Exodus 8:20), but that's where Moses is to stand before him. It isn't where the sacrifices go. Wilderness is the word.
Pharaoh doesn't mention speed, baker. His limit is about distance: "…you must not go very far." (Exodus 8:28) Nothing about how fast anybody goes. The word is far.

Not quite, baker. The LORD says He will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, so that no animal belonging to the Israelites will die. (Exodus 9:4) When it happens, the text says "…not one animal belonging to the Israelites died." (Exodus 9:6) That's zero, not a few.

That's right. The LORD sets a time and says, "Tomorrow the LORD will do this in the land." (Exodus 9:5) And the text says the next day He did just that. (Exodus 9:6) One word on the calendar, and the day delivers.

Yep, still stuck. Pharaoh sends officials and finds that none of the livestock of the Israelites had died. The text says, "But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not let the people go." (Exodus 9:7) The report is in, and the answer is still no. Wow.

I know, I was rooting for that one too, friend. But after his officials report back, the text says, "But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not let the people go." (Exodus 9:7) The officials found that none of Israel's livestock had died, and he still doesn't let them go. Hard one to read, but that's what it says.

That's it, baker. The LORD says, "It will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt…" (Exodus 9:9) Handfuls of soot go up in the air, and fine dust spreads over the land. Imagine flour over a whole country. And you thought my bakery was messy.

Smoke is a fair guess, since I've set off my share of kitchen smoke. But the LORD doesn't say smoke. He says the soot "…will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt…" (Exodus 9:9) Dust is the word.

Right, and it's a hard one to say out loud. The LORD says "…festering boils will break out on man and beast throughout the land." (Exodus 9:9) That covers people and animals alike. I think this part of the story hurts.

Gnats do show up earlier in this story, baker (Exodus 8:17), but that's a different plague. Here the LORD says "…festering boils will break out on man and beast throughout the land." (Exodus 9:9) The answer is boils.

That's what the text says. "The magicians could not stand before Moses, because the boils had broken out on them and on all the Egyptians." (Exodus 9:11) These are Pharaoh's magicians, and the boils reach them just like everyone else. I think that's a quiet kind of humbling.
